contract: §56m The tag names a note's front matter gives through its `tags:` lists, read as `tag::extract_frontmatter_tags` reads them: an inline list `tags: [a, b]` split at its commas, or the `- item` lines after a `tags:` line, indented or not, up to the first line that is not one; each entry trimmed, then its double and then its single quotes taken off, then every leading `#` (`tag::bare_tag`); empty names left out; case as written. `frontmatter` is the text between the two `---` lines, as `md::split_frontmatter` gives it. The Rust test `tag::frontmatter::tests::the_reader_agrees_with_the_shared_fixture` reads this file; another reader of front-matter tags (the app reads them in TypeScript too) can read it to agree. These are a line reader's answers, not a YAML parser's: where `yaml` 2.9.1 or `js-yaml` 4.3.2 rejects the text or reads a different value for the list (2026-10-26), `why` says so; a YAML value keeps the `#`s this reader takes off, which no case repeats. `cases` are front matters to read; `names` (see `names_contract`) are names to rename to. Every character outside ASCII is written as a JSON unicode escape.

cases.why: a double-quoted entry loses its quotes, then every leading # (tag::bare_tag): the body's #solo is the same tag
case is kept as written; the tag index lowercases after reading, the graph does not
a single-quoted entry, likewise
not YAML (# cannot begin a plain scalar), but read as written: the app's own tag writers have written such lines (they joined tags unquoted), and notes written that way keep them
an unquoted # after a comma, likewise: not YAML either
whitespace around the brackets and the commas is not part of a name
a name without # is read as it is
every leading # goes, not one
a nested tag keeps its /: the body's #a/b is the same tag
an entry is one name, whatever it holds: solo.x and my solo are not solo
an entry of only #s, or of nothing, names no tag and is left out (not YAML: the unquoted ## begins a comment)
block-list items, quoted
block-list items without #
a YAML comment (the item is null), read as written for the same reason as [#unq]
a nested tag in a block list
block items of only #s name no tag (to YAML the ## item is a comment, so null)
a block list at its key's own indentation, as YAML reads tags: followed by - solo
unindented items with CRLF line endings (yaml 2.9.1 keeps the last \r in the value: c\r)

cases.frontmatter:
aliases:
- x
tags:
- a
- b
related:
- x
- y
cases.why: a list ends at the first line that is not an item: the next key's - x items, and those of a key before tags:, are not tags
a list under another key is not tags
CRLF: a line is read without its line ending, and the last line keeps the \r before the closing ---, which is not part of the name (yaml 2.9.1 keeps it in the value: c\r)
the key is matched without case (to YAML this is the key Tags, which a lookup of tags would not find)
space before the colon
a block list under an upper-case key (to YAML this is the key TAGS, which a lookup of tags would not find)
Korean names, a hyphen inside one
a # in another field and a list under another key are not tags (to YAML the # begins a comment)

names_contract: `names`: new tag names, with their leading `#`s already off, and what `tag::rename_tag` does with each. `accepted` follows the rule on `rename_tag`: the body's reader reads `#name` back as the whole name, the name is not `-` alone, and not every character is default-ignorable. For an accepted name, `bare` is how it is written into a bare list entry (no quotes, no `#`): `frontmatter::yaml_string`, the frontend's `yamlString`, which quotes a spelling YAML would read as something other than this text. The Rust test `tag::frontmatter::tests::the_new_name_rule_agrees_with_the_shared_fixture` reads this section; the app's tag-name input can read it to agree. Every row uses characters old enough to be in every Unicode table the two languages ship.
